Run the reviewed one-command rollout and paste its output:

title: Guard review_open_ideas against backfill dispatches before any dated backfill runs
description:
`nodes/review_open_ideas.py` is the only node in the FX Research graph with **no backfill guard**. Every other projection node treats a non-empty `scrape_dates` as "this is a backfill for a historical date" and scopes its work accordingly. This one does not, so any dated backfill dispatch writes into live state.

```

title: Server must reject unauthenticated writes to /api/issues (401, not 201)
description:
## An unauthenticated write to `/api/issues*` returns 201 and is filed as Chris

Parent: [DIG-1254](/DIG/issues/DIG-1254). Root cause proved there by probe; this leaf is the server-side fix.

### The defect, reproduced

```
POST /api/issues/25a16d95-116c-4df5-a78d-a241d904cbdf/comments
(no Authorization header)
→ HTTP 201
→ { "authorType": "user", "authorUserId": "local-board",
    "authorAgentId": null, "onBehalfOfUserId": null,
    "createdByRunId": null, "metadata": null }
```

A write with **no credential at all** is accepted and permanently attributed to the board user. The server does not refuse it. That is the entire bug.

For contrast, with `Authorization: Bearer $PAPERCLIP_API_KEY` the same request returns 201 with `authorType: "agent"`, `authorAgentId` set and `createdByRunId` set — so **server-side attribution logic is already correct**. Do not go looking for an attribution bug. There is none.

The anti-spoofing guard also already exists: a body `onBehalfOfUserId` is refused with 422 *"Responsible user cannot be chosen by the caller (Server-derived attribution)."* That guard works and should be left alone.

title: IT: Supervisor has no backoff on repeated identical provider errors — rate-limit retries burn runs in tight loop
description:
## Problem

The supervisor retries provider errors with `scheduledRetryReason: "transient_failure"` in a tight loop (6 failures in 84 seconds observed). When a provider returns a hard quota refusal (rate limit) that will not clear — e.g., `opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` with 166 refusals over 450 minutes, 0 answered, recovery never observed — the retries burn runs for nothing.

Quota refusals return in 0.88-3.12s (median 1.28s), so retrying is not free and cannot succeed.

This is the second time a review-slot fill has been discovered by watching it fail in a loop (first was fledge-alpha-free, now muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free).

## Current behavior

- Provider returns rate limit error
- Supervisor marks as `transient_failure`
- Schedules retry with no/insufficient backoff
- Agent immediately retries and fails again

## Required

Add exponential backoff with jitter for repeated identical provider errors. After N consecutive identical errors (suggest N=3), treat as persistent and stop retrying, or escalate to IT.

title: CI guard: GLOOMBERB_ENABLED must never be set to an enabling value in a deployed config
description:
## The default-off flag is one env var away from being on, and nothing checks that

A regression test proves `gloomberb_enabled()` returns `False` when the variable is **absent**. It does not stop anyone setting `GLOOMBERB_ENABLED=1` on a deployed Worker, in a deployed `.env`, in a CI job that mirrors one, or in a `wrangler.toml` `[vars]` block. The [DIG-1233](/DIG/issues/DIG-1233) fix is a default, not a lock.

That matters more than usual here, because §14 says digithings has no organisational licence to use Gloomber at all. Chris accepted the risk for a **local experiment**. Flipping the flag on a deployed surface would put the prohibited access method in front of whoever reaches that surface, and it would void the acceptance on its own terms under lapse condition 2.

A CI check, in the repo, that fails when `GLOOMBERB_ENABLED` is set to an enabling value in any deployed configuration. `_env_flag` enables on exactly `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`, so those are the four values to reject, case-insensitively.

title: IT: Stop re-raise and re-wake on repeated refused disposition
description:
Build item 2 from DIG-1648.

**Problem:** When an assignee retries the same refused disposition (PATCH /api/issues/{id} with status), the platform re-raises the recovery action and re-wakes the assignee. DIG-534 shows 6 identical attempts between 2026-10-04T23:39 and 2026-10-06T20:55.

**Fix needed:** In the recovery action handler, detect repeated identical disposition attempts (same assignee, same status, same error) and escalate once instead of looping. After N identical refusals (suggest N=2), stop re-raising and either:
- Auto-escalate to board with a single notification
- Mark the recovery action as needing manual intervention

**Verification:** An assignee retrying a refused disposition gets one re-wake, then the loop stops and a single escalation occurs.

title: dt-books records a declared stamp on an FX row with no euro base, unchecked, and it cannot be taken back
description:
The books tool will record a declared stamp duty on a foreign-currency invoice that has **no euro base
at all**, and applies **no arithmetic check to it**. Found on the Invoicing Agent's probation run 3
(DIG-2395) and verified by me against the source line by line. Two halves, both real.

## Half 1 — `--stamp 2.00` on an FX row with no euro base is accepted unchecked

`~/paperclip-workspace/kit/bin/dt-books`, `stamp_decision` (~line 719):

```
above = None if amount_eur is None else amount_eur > threshold
```

Both contradiction checks are written `if above is not None and …`:

```
if above is not None and declared == 0.0 and above:      sys.exit(...)
if above is not None and declared > 0.0 and not above:  sys.exit(...)
```

So when `amount_eur is None`, `above` is `None`, **neither check runs**, and execution falls straight
through to `return f"{declared:.2f}", "declared"`. The declared figure goes into the row and into every
quarterly total with **nothing behind it but the free text of `--stamp-source`**.

The tool's docstring is not wrong — it says the figure is *"checked against the euro base when the euro
base is known"*, which is exactly true. **The gap is that the operator's

title: Paperclip adapter marks recovered ECONNRESET runs as failed (88% false positive)
description:
Route from DIG-2056 (IT lead routing call). The ECONNRESET false-failure is a **Paperclip runtime** defect, not a digithings-repo defect. Confirmed at source in `~/paperclip-fixes/pcsrc-8f8a0ab` @ `dd777f4b`, and verified live against the installed `@paperclipai/adapter-opencode-local` 2026.1001.0.

## The defect

`packages/adapters/opencode-local/src/server/parse.ts:88-103` accumulates **every** `error` frame seen anywhere in the JSONL stream into `errors[]`, then reports:

```ts
errorMessage: errors.length > 0 ? errors.join("
") : null,
```

There is no notion of whether the run continued after the error. `parseOpenCodeJsonl` is a stream reducer, but the fatal/non-fatal distinction it is being asked to make is a property of the **stream as a whole**, not of any single frame.

`packages/adapters/opencode-local/src/server/execute.ts:736-748` (`toResult`) then promotes that stale text into a failure:

```ts
const parsedError = typeof attempt.parsed.errorMessage === "string" ? attempt.parsed.errorMessage.trim() : "";
const synthesizedExitCode = parsedError && (rawExitCode ?? 0) === 0 ? 1 : rawExitCode;
...

title: Wire the worker dry-run build gate into develop's required checks
description:
Follow-up to the CTO second review on PR #5139. Raised there as: "DIG-995 must not be described as PRs-cannot-merge-broken-Workers until this lands."

## The gap, verified

`develop` branch protection requires exactly three contexts (queried from the branch-protection API):

- `Required checks passed`
- `doc-links + agents-init`
- `mypy — digibase + digikey`

`build-cloudflare-workers.yml` (added in #5139) is a standalone workflow file, not a job in `ci.yml`, so it never appears in `required-checks`'s `needs:` and is not a required context. A red Worker build is advisory: PRs merge with it failing. `required_approving_review_count` is also null and `enforce_admins` is false.

## Why this is not one `needs:` line

The drift guard at `ci.yml:665-683` exists precisely because the `needs:` list "went stale silently" once before. It parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and only that file. A standalone workflow is invisible to it — so the guard protecting the aggregator cannot see the job we would be adding to it. The guard must learn to scan all workflow files, or the job must move into `ci.yml`.

Found while fixing [DIG-2355](/DIG/issues/DIG-2355) (the IT journal append corruption). I ran the watchdog test suite before and after my change to prove I had not broken anything, and discovered the suite cannot answer that question: **its failure count moves with this machine's free disk space, not with the code.**

|---|---|---|

| 2 | **6** | **1** |

title: Validate interaction sourceRunId is bound to the interaction's own issue
description:
Platform fix for the third cause of continuation_source_context_missing, found while working DIG-2269.

POSTing an issue-thread interaction does not check that the creating run is bound to the issue the interaction is posted on. The interaction records the creating run as sourceRunId regardless.

- lines 99-100: if (sourceRunId && !sourceRun) throw new Error(explicitUserSource ? 'continuation_user_authorization_missing' : 'continuation_source_context_missing').

So the scoped lookup misses, sourceRun is null, and the continuation run dies at setup with providerWorkStarted:false. No agent action, no retry, no model switch and no worktree repair can fix it.

title: Platform defect: POST /api/issues/{id}/comments resets status to todo and silently reopens a done issue
description:
## Summary

`POST /api/issues/{id}/comments` **resets the issue status to `todo`**, including on an issue that is already `done`. Any agent that follows the natural order -- write the closing comment, then set `status: done` -- is fine. Any agent that sets `done` and *then* posts a summary comment **silently reopens its own closed issue**, and the response to the comment POST reports success.

This is the opposite of the documented intent of a comment. A comment on a finished issue should be inert.

## Reproduction

Against `DIG-1936`, board token, four observed states with one mutating call between each:

```
A  GET                     -> done
B  PATCH status=done       -> done
C  POST .../comments      -> todo      <-- comment POST returns 200 and reopens the issue
D  PATCH status=done       -> done
```

Between B and C the only mutating call was the comment POST. The `PATCH` at B is not lost: re-reading at B showed `done` still on the record, and the `PATCH` at D took effect immediately. So this is the comment, not a lost write.

## Why it matters

It is a silent closure failure, so it is invisible in the usual signals:

- The agent's final response says the issue is closed, and

title: DigiQuant publishes fills as trades: num_trades doubles every round trip on every backtest result
description:
Filed by R&D Lead from the weekly brief, 2026-10-07. Evidence is measured; the criteria are a proposal.
CTO owns the call — this is a child of DIG-427 because the code sits in the same function.

## The defect

`digiquant/src/digiquant/nautilus_runner.py:516-517` reads the engine's order-fill report and sets
`num_trades = len(fills)`. That counts **order fills**, not closed round trips. Line 629 sums the fill count
across symbols.

Measured on one run: 34 closed positions, 68 fills, published `num_trades = 68`. Every trades figure and every
`N=` printed beside a statistic on a DigiQuant backtest is double.

## Why this one matters more than a wrong number

This is the sample size. The strategy-agent design rule is "never print a rate without its N". A doubled N is
worse than a missing N: it halves the width of every confidence interval computed from it, so an honesty
envelope built on it reports more certainty than the run earned. A reader seeing `N=68` concludes 68 independent
observations when there were 34.

Environment: the monorepo, `nautilus_trader` 1.228.0 in `digiquant/.venv`, one process per run, data file

title: Correct policy section 2: git cherry is not squash-invariant, and the census inflates tier counts
description:
## Why

The census that tiers stranded branches measures "unmerged patches" with
`git cherry origin/develop origin/<branch> | grep -c '^+'`, and
`docs/ops/branch-hygiene-policy.md` §2 states that this measure is
invariant to squash, rebase and reorder. That claim is wrong for squash merges,
and the wrongness inflated the census that [DIG-1580](/DIG/issues/DIG-1580) just
acted on.

## The defect, with a worked example

`task/4311-gitleaks-env-example-gap`:

- PR #4320 MERGED on 2026-09-17. Merge commit `891eba9a5` has a **single
  parent** — it is a squash merge — and **is an ancestor of `origin/develop`**.
- Yet `git cherry` reports all 3 of its commits as `+` (unmerged), and none of
  the 3 branch shas are ancestors of develop.

Squash collapses N commits into ONE commit whose patch-id is the *combined* diff.
The individual commit patch-ids then match nothing on develop, so every one of
them is reported as unmerged forever. `git cherry` is invariant to rebase and
reorder, but **not** to squash. The policy text asserts otherwise.

## Consequence for the census

All 35 T2 branches with merged PRs had **single-parent squash** merge commits
(not true merge commits). Every one of them

title: Disk at 84%: Paperclip DB dump dir is 15 GB across 69 unpruned hourly dumps
description:
Raised by DIG-1550 (DevOps stranded-work and backup report).

`~/.paperclip/instances/default/data/backups` holds **15 GB across 69 hourly dumps**, each ~446-448 MB. The Oct 3 dumps were ~137 KB. Growth per day: Oct 3 = 284 K; Oct 4 = 608 M; Oct 5 = 4.9 G; Oct 6 = 9.1 G in 21 h. That is roughly 10 GB/day and accelerating.

The data volume is at **84% capacity** (926 GiB total, 749 GiB used, 152 GiB free).

Why this is IT's call: the dump directory belongs to Paperclip, and `dt-backup`'s `KEEP_DAYS=14` prunes only `dt-backup`'s own archives - **nothing prunes Paperclip's dumps**. `dt-backup` embeds the newest dump, so our encrypted archive has tripled in three days (35 M -> 140 M -> 465 M) purely because of this directory.

I have deleted nothing: 15 GB is destructive and the directory is not mine.

**What I need:** a retention policy for Paperclip's own dumps (keep N most recent, or keep 1/day), and either a cleanup run or a change that makes retention automatic. I will re-run `dt-backup` afterwards and confirm the archive size and free space recover.

Follow-up to DIG-1346. The local_trusted write guard is live on this instance as a hotfix inside an installed npm package (`@paperclipai/server@2026.1001.0`, `dist/middleware/auth.js`, sha256 `34805869576e447a5533aca93e75f144cd2241996b65969db7f8f6db6ad0da8f`).

## The risk

The next `paperclipai update` replaces that file and the guard is **gone with no error**. No crash, no warning, no changed behaviour that anyone would notice from the outside — writes simply start being accepted again as the board user.

This is worse than a failure, because a failure announces itself. `~/paperclip-fixes/dig-1346/activate-local-hotfix.sh` fails **closed** on a sha mismatch, so an upgrade cannot corrupt a file the patch was not built against. But nothing checks that the guard is *present*, only that the file is not unexpectedly changed.

## Why the upstream fix does not close this

The fix is open as https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15303 (fork `chrizefan/paperclip`). It is a contributor PR from an account with no standing in the project. It may sit unreviewed for a long time. Until it merges and ships, the guard's lifetime here is exactly the time to the next CLI upgrade.

title: digifetch seam: cross-origin header leak on redirect, and 307/308 drop the POST body
description:
Two defects in the shared fetch seam `digifetch/src/digifetch/http.py`,
`HttpFetcher.fetch`. Found by the CTO while reviewing
[DIG-1072](/DIG/issues/DIG-1072) / PR #5142. **Both predate that PR; that PR
only puts a body-bearing POST onto the seam for the first time, which makes
both reachable in a new place.**

Neither blocks PR #5142: `EXA_API_BASE` there is the hardcoded constant
`https://api.exa.ai`, so neither is attacker-reachable through that call site
today. Both matter as soon as any consumer passes a user-influenced URL.

## 1. Cross-origin credential leak on redirect (higher)

`fetch` forwards per-call `headers` to **every** hop, including cross-origin
ones. It deliberately origin-scopes `cookies` — the class docstring says "a
cross-origin redirect drops them instead of leaking a session credential" — but
applies no equivalent rule to headers. So any credential passed as a header
follows the redirect off-origin.

Reproduction (executed, `httpx.MockTransport`, no network):

```python
with HttpFetcher(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)) as f:
    f.fetch("https://api.exa.ai/search", method="POST", json={"query": "q"},
            headers={"x-api-key": "exa_live_SECRET"}

Add one line to the root `.gitignore` of `~/paperclip-workspace/kit`:

That is the whole change. It is a 1-line, add-only, no-conflict-risk edit to a tracked file.

Security already dropped `secrets/.gitignore` (containing `*`) inside the directory, so in this

This matters more than usual right now: a conflict resolution that stages the tree is precisely
how an ignored-but-unlisted path gets swept in. A root entry survives that; an inner one does too,

description:
Filing-pack risk. Raising this directly rather than leaving it in a rules file, because it is the first time a CONFIRMED rule in `engine/rules/2026.yaml` has been found to rest on text that is no longer the law.

## The finding

`forfettario_tax_rate_startup_duration_years = 5` (years) is marked CONFIRMED, sourced to **Legge 23 dicembre 2014, n. 190, art. 1, comma 65**, quoting verbatim:

> «per il periodo d'imposta in cui l'attivita' e' iniziata e per i **quattro successivi**»

and carrying `would_change_if: "Nothing expected"`.

**That quote is the pre-2017 text.** A five-year preferential window is what comma 65 said *before* L. 97/2017. After L. 97/2017 the preferential window is shorter, and the 5% is additionally permanent for qualifying under-40s. **So 5 years is LIKELY WRONG for 2026.**

Its own `confirmed_by` reads `tax-specialist (primary source read 2026-10-04)`. I read that article myself, and the payload I got was the 2014 original, not consolidated text. I did not notice at the time.

title: issue_blockers_resolved re-fires forever on issues blocked on an out-of-band human action
description:
## The gap

An issue blocked on something a person does outside Paperclip has **no unresolved blocker edges**, so the resolver sees nothing outstanding and fires `issue_blockers_resolved` on every sweep. Each firing resets the issue from `blocked` to `in_progress`, so finished work reopens and has to be re-verified, forever.

## Evidence

DIG-1900, three consecutive firings, blocker unresolved every time:

- wake 1 (9th pass) — `ledger/config.json` unchanged
- wake 2 (10th pass) — same file, same mtime 2026-10-07T23:42:09Z
- wake 3 (11th pass) — same mtime, still NOT REGISTERED

Mechanism visible in wake 3: `blockedTransitionAt 2026-10-08T13:06:06.095Z`, then `updatedAt 13:07:03`, status `in_progress`.

## Why it cannot be worked around

The only mechanism for recording an out-of-band blocker is `unblockDescriptor`, and **an agent may only name itself as unblock owner** — naming a human returns 403 `Agents may only name themselves as an unblock owner`. So the agent cannot mark "waiting on Chris" in a form the resolver respects, and must name itself to record any disposition at all.

description:

The fix belongs to the routine executor: pin a target issue and wake it rather than mint a new one.
